title: CHAPTER 7: FOREIGN TRADE AND BALANCE OF PAYMENTS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Balance of Payments (BoP) is a systematic record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world during a given time period.
The Current Account records visible trade (goods), invisible trade (services), primary income (dividends/interest), and secondary transfers (remittances).
The Capital Account records transactions that change the stock of foreign assets and liabilities, including FDI, FPI, External Commercial Borrowings (ECB), and banking capital.
India practices a Managed Floating Exchange Rate system, where market forces determine the rate while the Reserve Bank of India intervenes to curb excessive volatility.
Special Drawing Rights (SDR) is an international reserve asset created by the IMF, based on a basket of five major currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP).

blocks.content: Balance of Payments is a systematic record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world over a specified period.

rows: Flow of income, goods, and services
Flow of capital assets and liabilities
Does not directly alter future asset/liability stocks
Directly changes ownership of national/foreign assets
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), FPI, loans (ECB), NRI deposits
Partial convertibility (managed via Tarapore Committee guidelines)

items: Remittances are classified under the Invisibles section of the Current Account, NOT the Capital Account.
REER vs NEER: Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) adjusts the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) for inflation differentials between trading partners.
Autonomous transactions ('above-the-line') occur for economic self-interest, whereas Accommodating transactions ('below-the-line') are undertaken to bridge the BoP deficit or surplus.
